draft.title: Sustainable city strategies
card: A sustainable city meets the needs of people today without harming the environment or the chances of people in the future. It aims to use fewer resources and make less pollution.
Public transport and cycleways give people a way to travel that is not a private car. Fewer car trips can mean less air pollution and fewer greenhouse gas emissions.
Parks and tree cover give shade and cool the air. Trees can also soak up some pollution, and green space gives habitat for wildlife.
Energy-efficient buildings use less electricity for heating, cooling and lighting. Cutting waste, by reusing and recycling, means less rubbish goes to landfill.
draft.remember: Sustainable cities use less energy, travel by car less, keep more green space and make less waste.

a.q: Which action would help a city become more sustainable by reducing the number of car trips?
opts: Building a new cycleway along a main road
Planting more trees in a local park
Adding insulation to an office building
Starting a recycling program in schools
a.why: A cycleway gives people a way to travel that is not a car, so some car trips can be replaced. Trees, insulation and recycling are sustainable actions too, but they work on heat, energy use and waste, not on car trips.
a.clue: Which option gives people a different way to get around?

b.q: On hot summer days, a western Sydney council finds its streets are much hotter than its leafy parks. Which strategy would most directly cool the streets?
opts: Increasing tree cover along the streets
Running more buses on the main roads
Building a cycleway to the town centre
b.why: Trees give shade and cool the air, so more tree cover along streets can lower the heat there. More buses and cycleways can cut car pollution, and recycling cuts waste, but none of these gives shade to the street.
b.clue: Which strategy gives shade and cools the air?

a.best: Building a new cycleway along a main road

b.best: Increasing tree cover along the streets
